title: Conversational Cost‑Fidelity Sculptor: runtime advisor and onramp design
author: Marisol Gomez
body:
Summary
-------
This design describes the Conversational Cost‑Fidelity Sculptor (the Sculptor): a runtime advisor and developer onramp feature that automatically derives per‑route cost/fidelity tradeoffs, recommends conservative defaults, and offers programmatic hooks to negotiate fidelity at request time. The Sculptor aims to reduce unit cost by 15–40% for typical conversational workloads with minimal impact to customer‑observed quality.

Goals
-----
- Provide a runtime component that scores fidelity vs cost for each conversational route and suggests a safe default profile.
- Expose an API SDK that allows developers to accept, override, or negotiate fidelity at call‑time.
- Integrate with Optimize recommendations to propose quantization and caching profiles per tenant.
- Ship an onramp playbook to migrate high‑usage tenants with one‑click conservative rollout (canary → warm → global).

Non‑Goals
---------
- This design does not replace Eval suites or manual A/B fidelity testing (those remain required for high‑safety verticals).
- Sculptor will not change model weights or apply dynamic quantization at inference time; it recommends quant profiles and manages variant selection.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
Customers often face a difficult tradeoff: keep high fidelity to preserve UX, or reduce compute (and cost) with caching, batching, or lower‑fidelity variants. Existing tooling provides cost numbers and static recommendations, but lacks a runtime negotiator that:
1) maps fidelity dimensions to measurable cost deltas,
2) provides safe runtime fallbacks, and
3) offers a smooth onramp for customers to adopt conservative defaults with measurable rollback.

Design overview
---------------
The Sculptor has three logical layers:
1) Profiling & Cost Modeling (offline): builds per‑route fidelity profiles and cost delta models from synthetic traffic and shadow evaluator results.
2) Runtime Scoring & Decisioning: a lightweight service in the request path that returns a fidelity profile and route routing hint.
3) Developer API / Onramp UX: SDK + Console flows to accept/reject suggestions, preview cost impacts, and run staged rollouts.

Key principles
- Conservative by default: suggested profiles must be quality‑preserving for 95% of a tenant's sampled prompts before wide rollout.
- Explainable recommendations: every suggested change includes an expected token reduction, latency delta, and signal provenance.
- Rollback safe: runtime supports automatic revert thresholds and per‑route canary windows.

Components and interactions
---------------------------
- Sculptor Profiler (batch job): runs shadow evaluations per tenant route using representative prompt sets. Outputs: fidelity profiles, measured token deltas, regression risk score, recommended quant + cache policies.
- Sculptor Scoring API (runtime): low‑latency microservice co‑located with routing plane. Input: route id, tenant id, sample token distribution header. Output: fidelity_profile_id, expected_cost_delta_pct, traces for observability. TTL: 60s cached.
- Sculptor Orchestrator (control plane): stores profiles, coordinates rollouts, integrates with Console/Optimize.
- Client SDK: exposes negotiation primitives: acceptProfile(), requestNegotiation(preferred_cost_pct), previewEstimate().

API contract (example)
---------------------
Request (JSON over gRPC/REST):
{
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "route_id": "string",
  "sequence_length_hint": 128,
  "latency_slo_ms": 300,
  "quality_floor": "accuracy:0.92|intent:0.95"
}

Response:
{
  "fidelity_profile_id": "string",
  "components": ["kv_cache:prefix", "model_variant:opt-quant-8", "batch_hint:32"],
  "estimated_cost_delta_pct": "-26",
  "regression_risk": "low",
  "explainers": ["shadow-eval:2026-06-12-tenant-sample-12", "trace:profiler-run-013"]
}

Configuration table (control plane knobs)
----------------------------------------
| key | type | default | description |
| sculptor.enabled | boolean | true | Global on/off for recommendation serving |
| sculptor.max_cost_reduction_pct | integer | 40 | Hard cap on suggested cost reductions per tenant |
| sculptor.quality_guardrail | string | "0.90:0.90" | Minimum pass thresholds (f1:precision) for auto‑apply |
| sculptor.canary_window_minutes | integer | 60 | Time window for canary before auto‑expand |
| sculptor.trace_sample_rate | float | 0.02 | Fraction of requests that emit detailed explainers |

Profile schema (flat key set)
----------------------------
- id (string)
- display_name (string)
- component_list (comma separated string, e.g. "kv_cache:prefix,model_variant:opt-quant-8")
- expected_cost_delta_pct (string)
- measured_regression_risk (string: low/medium/high)
- created_by (string)
- created_at (YYYY-MM-DD)

Runtime placement and performance constraints
-------------------------------------------
- The Sculptor Scoring API must add <= 3ms p50 latency to an already instrumented routing path when cached.
- Cold scoring (cache miss) target p50: <= 12ms, p95: <= 50ms.
- Memory: scoring service is stateless; profiles are read‑through cached in local memcache.
- Backpressure behaviour: if scoring unavailable, the router falls back to tenant default profile and emits an observability tag.

Observability and telemetry
--------------------------
- Trace fields: sculptor.profile.id, sculptor.estimate.delta_pct, sculptor.regression_risk, sculptor.decision_source.
- Metrics (per tenant/route): suggestions_applied_count, suggestion_rejected_count, estimated_savings_tokens, observed_tokens_saved, quality_regressions_detected.
- SLOs: recommendation correctness (measured by shadow eval convergence) 95% within predicted delta ±10% across the canary cohort.

Operational playbook (runbook summary)
-------------------------------------
1) Enabling Sculptor for tenant: enable feature flag -> run profiler job -> review recommended profiles in Console -> start 5% canary.
2) Canary monitoring: watch estimated vs observed token delta, shadow eval pass rate, customer error rate.
3) Auto‑expand: if no regressions after canary_window and observed_savings within 10% of estimate, expand to 25% then 100%.
4) Rollback: if quality_regressions_detected > 0 or latency breaches, automatically revert changes and notify SE.

Safety checks and quality guardrails
----------------------------------
- Shadow evaluation: all profiles must have a shadow eval sample (N>=200) and regression_risk != high before auto‑apply.
- Human reviewer path: for any tenant in regulated verticals (labels: healthcare, finance), require product owner approval.
- Canary drift detector: compares shadow eval metrics vs production signals; triggers abort if drift > threshold.

Developer SDK examples
----------------------
- Node SDK snippet:
```js
const sculptor = new SculptorClient();
const rec = await sculptor.getRecommendation({tenantId, routeId, sequenceLengthHint: 64});
if (rec.regression_risk === 'low') {
  client.call({routeId, fidelityProfile: rec.fidelity_profile_id});
} else {
  client.call({routeId}); // fallback to tenant default
}
```
- Server negotiation flow (pseudocode):
1. Request recommendation with latencySLO and qualityFloor.
2. If estimated_cost_delta_pct <= allowed budget → accept.
3. Else call previewEstimate() to show developer; allow explicit override.

Rollout plan and milestones
---------------------------
- M0 (2026‑07): Profiler baseline implementation + sample job.
- M1 (2026‑09): Scoring API v1 + SDK hooks (internal limited tenants).
- M2 (2026‑11): Console integration + canary automation.
- M3 (2027‑01): Optimize integration (recommend quant/caching profiles) + GA for self‑serve tenants.

Metrics to measure success
-------------------------
- Unit economics: mean token cost reduction per tenant (target 15–40%).
- Quality: rate of detected regressions (target < 1% of routes per month).
- Adoption: fraction of active tenants with Sculptor engaged (target 30% within 6 months of GA).

Ownership and stakeholders
-------------------------

- Engineering lead: Ethan Clarke (eng-platform)
- Applied ML / Eval contributor: Priya Nambiar (applied-ml-and-evals)
- SRE integration: Liam O'Neill (eng-sre)

Open questions
--------------
- Should the profiler run continuous background sampling for high‑variance routes or only periodic jobs?
- How to attribute savings for multi‑route sessions that share KV cache benefits?
- What customer telemetry opt‑in model is required for privacy‑sensitive tenants?

Appendix: Example console UX copy
--------------------------------
Title: "Sculptor recommended cost‑saving profile"
Body: "We analyzed recent traffic for Route Payments/checkout and recommend a 22% token reduction using a prefix KV cache plus an 8‑bit model variant. Estimated impact: $X/mo savings at your current volume. We ran a shadow test on 300 representative prompts; expected regression risk: low. Start a 1‑hour canary at 5% traffic."

Notes
-----
